# schema.ts is regenerated by CI from a chain-built Postgres, in a stable order (#404)

## Context and Problem Statement
issue #404. The committed file had been hand-edited whenever no `DATABASE_URL` reached the authoring container, so a real introspect rewrote ~300 lines. drizzle-kit orders output by catalog row order, which `VACUUM FULL` changes on an unchanged database, so a plain regeneration is not reproducible; sorting makes the file a pure function of the schema. Building from the chain rather than introspecting the shared `dev` branch removes `dev` drift as a confound (D333).

## Decision Drivers
Rationale unknown — backfill pending.

## Considered Options
Rationale unknown — backfill pending.

## Decision Outcome
Chosen option: "`.github/workflows/schema.yml` builds a Postgres 16 from `database/migrations/` and `database/seeds/` on every relevant push to `main`, runs `scripts/refresh-schema.sh` (drizzle-kit introspect, `app/scripts/normalize-schema.ts`, Prettier) and opens or updates a `chore/schema-refresh` PR when `app/src/db/schema.ts` differs. The normaliser sorts declarations and import specifiers by name. Landing the PR is one human merge, as for the graph (D289).".

### Consequences
`npm run db:introspect` now runs `scripts/refresh-schema.sh`, so `validate:app` regenerates the sorted file instead of writing raw drizzle-kit output; bare `drizzle-kit introspect` must not write into the repo. A schema change may still hand-edit `schema.ts` so its own PR's tests pass, and the refresh PR reconciles it after merge. A new Postgres major version changes `pg_get_viewdef` aliasing, so the image tag is pinned.
